builder_plan.scenario: Your inference service slows down when several customers send requests together.
builder_plan.change: Replay a recorded request trace with only the proposed serving policy changed.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current scheduler on the same model and hardware.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Requests meeting your latency target, throughput, failures, and cost per successful request.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Scalable Placement for Disaggregated LLM Serving on Heterogeneous Edge Fleets
summary: Spade replaces genetic-search or exhaustive placement planning for disaggregated prefill/decode LLM serving with a dominance-pruned combinatorial search combining water-filling layer partitioning and a bounded multidimensional knapsack under a congestion-aware objective. The cost is implementing a custom planner: the device model, dominance-pruning logic, and knapsack solver must be integrated into the serving stack and re-run when fleet composition or demand shifts. It can fail when real workloads deviate from the synthetic bursty-demand model used for evaluation, when the fleet is too small or homogeneous for disaggregation to pay off, or when the objective's congestion proxy misestimates actual queueing latency.
rationale: The method targets operators of heterogeneous edge fleets running disaggregated LLM serving, an infrastructure setting the reader does not have, though the congestion-aware placement formulation is worth tracking if they later manage multi-device deployments.
technique: Pruned combinatorial placement for disaggregated edge LLM serving

claims.statement: Spade replaces genetic-search or exhaustive placement planning for disaggregated prefill/decode LLM serving with a dominance-pruned combinatorial search combining water-filling layer partitioning and a bounded multidimensional knapsack under a congestion-aware objective. The cost is implementing a custom planner: the device model, dominance-pruning logic, and knapsack solver must be integrated into the serving stack and re-run when fleet composition or demand shifts. It can fail when real workloads deviate from the synthetic bursty-demand model used for evaluation, when the fleet is too small or homogeneous for disaggregation to pay off, or when the objective's congestion proxy misestimates actual queueing latency.

On a 30-device synthetic fleet, Spade finds the optimal placement in 441 ms versus roughly two hours for a genetic-search baseline with dynamic-programming partitioning, whose solution is also 19.7% worse on the congestion objective; pruning eliminates 99.6% of candidates while matching exhaustive enumeration.
